newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Prices slip in bearish market.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Prices slip in bearish market.

text.p: Weaker overnight crudes nudged light distillate prices down on Friday amid little resistance from weak fundamentals.
Japanese open-spec naphtha levels for September 1-15 fell overnight to $199/$200 per tonne from $201.75/$203.00 while Singapore swaps for July shed 30 cents per barrel to $20.50/$20.70.
"The market is bearish until at least October," a South Korean trader said. "The contango is getting wider."
Traders' supplies were ample amid high stocks and arbitrage supplies.
Western traders have fixed cargoes from the Mediterranean to arrive in Asia late August, traders said.
Weak prices in the West, coupled with with low freight rates was keeping the arbitrage window open, and threatening the market with even more supplies.
"Buyers are very quiet...most have tank top situations and are doing time swaps amongst themselves," a South Korean seller said.

Adding to the surplus on the prompt market is a fresh tender from state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC), offering 25,000 tonnes of low aromatic naphtha (LAN) lifting July 20-22 from Bombay on the west coast, industry sources said.
The tender closes July 10 and is valid until July 11.
Gasoline was also bearish with little demand other than Taiwan's usual tender for second-half August requirments in a tender closing on July 9.
Supplies are expected to rise as the region heads out of the peak demand season and exports from South Korea resume amid high stocks.
"There are high stocks of gasoline, but it is not a problem and we will only have export avails in September,' said one South Korean refiner.

For the third quarter, state-owned Vietnam National Petroleum Import-Export Corp (Petrolimex) bought by tender four 18,000-tonne cargoes of 83-octane leaded gasoline of Russian origin at a lower price than its second quarter purchases.

It paid 70-cents per barrel over Singapore spot naphtha quotes, c-and-f Ho Chi Minh City, Danang or Hongai to Singapore trader Kuo Oil International for two cargoes and Mitsui and Daxin for a cargo each.
One cargo each will be delivered in July and September and two cargoes in August.
Sources said Petrolimex is in talks for two more gasoline cargoes of Russian origin, which they said were difficult to come by.
In its last tender, Vietnam took six 18,000-tonne gasoline cargoes at 80-cents premium to Singapore spot naphtha quotes, c-and-f basis.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
